**[Section 2 --- Subject Property Identification]{.underline}**

**Property Name:** The Piedmont at Brightleaf

**Street Address:** 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701

**Parcel Identification Numbers:** Parcel 0821-04-72-3341 (601 Foster Street) and Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 (615 Foster Street). Both parcels are recorded in the Office of the Durham County Register of Deeds and are reflected on the Durham County tax maps.

**Total Land Area:** The subject property consists of two contiguous parcels totaling approximately 3.47 acres, or approximately 151,153 square feet. The parcels are being developed as a single integrated site under unified ownership.

**Shape and Topography:** The combined site is irregular in shape, with approximately 420 feet of frontage along Foster Street on the western boundary. The topography is generally level with a slight grade change of approximately four feet from the northern boundary to the southern boundary, sloping gently to the south. The grade differential is not considered significant and is accommodated within the proposed site plan and building design without extraordinary foundation or grading costs.

**Current Condition:** The site is vacant improved land. Former tobacco warehouse structures that previously occupied both parcels were demolished in August 2024 pursuant to demolition permits issued by the City of Durham. Environmental remediation activities associated with a former underground storage tank on Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 were completed in September 2024, as further described in Section 8 of this report. As of the date of inspection, the site has been cleared of all structures and debris and has been rough-graded in preparation for construction.

**Frontage and Access:** The property has approximately 420 feet of frontage along Foster Street, a two-lane paved public roadway with on-street parking and sidewalks. Secondary vehicular access is available from a 20-foot public alley along the eastern boundary of the site. The proposed site plan incorporates a primary vehicular entrance from Foster Street and a secondary entrance and loading/service access from the public alley to the east.

**Utilities:** All municipal utilities are available to the site, including municipal water and sewer service provided by the City of Durham Department of Water Management, electric service provided by Duke Energy Carolinas, natural gas service provided by Dominion Energy North Carolina, and telecommunications and fiber-optic service from multiple providers.

**Flood Zone:** The subject property is located in Flood Zone X (area of minimal flood hazard) as depicted on the Federal Emergency Management Agency Flood Insurance Rate Map (\"FIRM\"), Community Panel Number 3710406400J, with an effective date of May 2, 2019. No portion of the site lies within a Special Flood Hazard Area, and flood insurance is not required by federal regulation.

**Zoning:** The property is zoned MU-D (Mixed Use --- Downtown) under the City of Durham Unified Development Ordinance. The MU-D zoning classification permits residential, retail, office, and mixed-use structures by right, with a maximum building height of 120 feet. The proposed development, at six stories and approximately 78 feet in height, is well within the applicable height limitation. Minimum parking requirements under the MU-D district have been satisfied by the proposed structured parking garage providing 276 spaces. No variances, special use permits, or conditional use approvals are required for the proposed development as currently designed.

**Tax Assessment:** The current combined assessed value of the two parcels, as reflected on the Durham County tax rolls following the post-demolition reassessment, is \$7,250,000 (land value only). The Durham County Tax Identification Numbers correspond to the parcel identification numbers referenced above. Property taxes for the 2024 tax year are current and paid.

**Ownership:** The subject property is owned by Harborview Capital Partners LLC, a North Carolina limited liability company, organized and existing under the laws of the State of North Carolina, NC Secretary of State File Number 1923847, with principal offices at 400 West Main Street, Suite 310, Durham, North Carolina 27701. The managing member of Harborview Capital Partners LLC is Elena Vasquez-Torres.

**Recorded Encumbrances: The appraiser reviewed the preliminary title commitment prepared by Aldersgate Title & Escrow Inc. (Commitment Number NC-2024-88712, dated December 5, 2024). Although the title commitment is dated subsequent to the effective date of the appraisal, it was reviewed for completeness and to confirm the status of encumbrances of record. The following encumbrances were noted:**

> \(a\) A 20-foot utility easement along the western boundary of the combined site, benefiting Duke Energy Carolinas, for the purpose of installing, maintaining, and repairing overhead and underground utility lines and related infrastructure;
>
> \(b\) A stormwater management easement in favor of the City of Durham, recorded in Book 7421, Page 212, Durham County Register of Deeds, affecting approximately 0.22 acres in the southern portion of the site and requiring maintenance of stormwater detention and conveyance facilities;
>
> \(c\) A Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (\"CC&Rs\") recorded in Book 6984, Page 1155, Durham County Register of Deeds, imposed by the Brightleaf Historic District Association, Inc., establishing architectural review and design standards applicable to all new construction and major exterior modifications within the Brightleaf Historic District; and
>
> \(d\) A deed of trust in favor of Triangle Commercial Bank, recorded in 2018, with an original principal amount of \$3,400,000, encumbering both parcels.

The appraiser\'s analysis assumes that the encumbrances described in items (a), (b), and (c) above do not materially affect the development potential or value of the property. The proposed site plan accommodates the utility easement and stormwater management easement, and the architectural design has been reviewed and approved by the Brightleaf Historic District Association in accordance with the CC&Rs. With respect to item (d), the appraiser assumes that the existing deed of trust in favor of Triangle Commercial Bank will be satisfied and released prior to or concurrently with the closing of the proposed construction financing.

**[Section 3 --- Project Description]{.underline}**

**Developer:** Harborview Capital Partners LLC, a North Carolina limited liability company, with Elena Vasquez-Torres serving as Managing Member. The developer has a demonstrated track record in the Triangle market, having completed four prior mixed-use residential and commercial development projects in the Raleigh-Durham area totaling approximately \$128 million in aggregate development costs. Prior projects include The Edison at West Village (84 units, Durham, completed 2019), The Meridian on Glenwood (116 units, Raleigh, completed 2020), Harborview Lofts (64 units, Chapel Hill, completed 2021), and The Apex at Chatham (92 units, Cary, completed 2023).

**Architect:** Meridian Design Collective PC, a North Carolina professional corporation with offices in Durham, North Carolina. The firm specializes in urban infill, mixed-use, and multifamily residential design, with particular expertise in the historic districts of downtown Durham.

**General Contractor:** Graystone Construction Group Inc., a North Carolina corporation, NC General Contractor License Number 78442, with principal offices at 1200 Fayetteville Road, Raleigh, North Carolina 27603. The president of the firm is Mark D. Sullivan. The construction contract is a guaranteed maximum price (\"GMP\") contract with a total GMP of \$34,750,000. The GMP contract has been executed and a copy was provided to the appraiser for review.

**Project Type:** The proposed project is a ground-up construction of a Class A mixed-use residential and retail development to be known as \"The Piedmont at Brightleaf.\"

**Total Gross Building Area:** Approximately 287,500 square feet.

**Stories:** The building will consist of six stories --- five residential floors above a one-story podium level containing ground-floor retail space and a four-level structured parking garage.

**Residential Unit Mix:** The project will contain a total of 212 residential rental units distributed as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Unit Type**     **Number of Units**   **Average Unit Size (SF)**   **Total Residential SF**
  ----------------- --------------------- ---------------------------- --------------------------
  One-Bedroom       142                   725                          102,950

  Two-Bedroom       56                    1,050                        58,800

  Three-Bedroom     14                    1,350                        18,900

  **Total**         **212**               **--- ---**                  **180,650**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Retail Space:** The ground-floor podium level will include approximately 18,400 square feet of retail space configured across seven individual retail bays. The bays range in size from approximately 1,800 square feet to 3,600 square feet and are designed for neighborhood-serving commercial uses, including restaurants, cafes, personal services, and boutique retail. The retail spaces will feature floor-to-ceiling glass storefronts, direct street access from Foster Street, and independent HVAC and utility metering.

**Parking:** The project includes a four-level structured parking garage integrated into the podium level, providing a total of 276 parking spaces, representing a ratio of approximately 1.30 spaces per residential unit. The parking allocation includes 18 dedicated retail parking spaces, 14 ADA-accessible spaces, and 22 electric vehicle charging stations equipped with Level 2 charging infrastructure. Access to the parking garage will be controlled by a card-access system with separate entrances for residential and retail/visitor parking.

**Amenities:** The project will feature a comprehensive amenity package consistent with Class A apartment communities in the downtown Durham market, including:

> • Rooftop terrace with outdoor kitchen, fire pit, and lounge seating areas;
>
> • Fitness center (approximately 2,800 square feet) with cardio, strength, and yoga studio areas;
>
> • Co-working lounge (approximately 1,500 square feet) with private meeting rooms and high-speed internet;
>
> • Resort-style pool deck with sundeck and cabanas;
>
> • Dog park with pet wash station;
>
> • Secured package room with automated locker system;
>
> • Bicycle storage room with capacity for 48 bicycles and a bicycle repair station;
>
> • Controlled-access building entry with intercom system and 24-hour video surveillance.

**Building Construction:** The building will be Type III-A construction, consisting of a wood-frame superstructure over a reinforced concrete podium. The foundation system will consist of a reinforced concrete mat foundation supported on driven piles, based on geotechnical recommendations provided by Carolina Geotechnical Associates. Exterior materials will include a combination of brick veneer, fiber cement panels, and aluminum curtain wall glazing systems, designed to be consistent with the Brightleaf Historic District architectural standards and the requirements of the CC&Rs. Interior unit finishes will be Class A quality, including quartz countertops, stainless steel appliances, luxury vinyl plank flooring, and in-unit washer and dryer connections.

**Projected Construction Timeline:** Construction is projected to commence upon closing of the construction loan and is estimated to require approximately 30 months from commencement to substantial completion. Projected substantial completion is August 31, 2027.

**Total Project Costs:** The total estimated project cost is \$56,700,000, as set forth in the developer\'s detailed development budget reviewed by the appraiser. The budget is summarized as follows:

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Cost Category**                                              **Amount**
  -------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Land Acquisition                                               \$8,200,000

  Hard Construction Costs (GMP)                                  \$34,750,000

  Soft Costs (architecture, engineering, permits, legal, etc.)   \$4,150,000

  Interest Reserve                                               \$4,850,000

  Origination Fee                                                \$475,000

  Developer Fee                                                  \$2,835,000

  Contingency                                                    \$1,440,000

  **Total Project Costs**                                        **\$56,700,000**
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Financing:** The developer has obtained a commitment for a \$47,500,000 senior construction loan from Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. (the subject of this appraisal engagement) and a \$9,200,000 mezzanine loan from Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC. The developer\'s equity contribution, inclusive of the value of the land, is projected to comprise the balance of the capital stack.

**[Section 4 --- Market Analysis Summary]{.underline}**

**[Durham Multifamily Market Overview]{.underline}**

Durham, North Carolina, has experienced robust population and employment growth over the past decade, driven principally by the expansion of the Research Triangle\'s technology, healthcare, biotechnology, and life sciences sectors. The Durham-Chapel Hill Metropolitan Statistical Area (\"MSA\") population has grown at an annualized rate of approximately 2.1% over the past five years, outpacing both the national average and the average for the state of North Carolina. The city\'s economic base is anchored by major employers including Duke University, the Duke University Health System, IBM, Hartleigh Investments, and numerous biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies clustered in and around Research Triangle Park.

Downtown Durham, in particular, has undergone significant revitalization over the past fifteen years, with substantial public and private investment transforming the American Tobacco, Brightleaf, and West Village districts into vibrant mixed-use neighborhoods. The redevelopment of historic tobacco warehouses and surrounding properties has attracted a critical mass of residential, retail, restaurant, and entertainment uses that have established downtown Durham as one of the most desirable urban neighborhoods in the Research Triangle region.

**[Competitive Submarket]{.underline}**

The subject property is located within the downtown Durham / Brightleaf submarket. As of the third quarter of 2024, the submarket contained approximately 4,850 Class A multifamily rental units across 14 properties. Overall Class A vacancy in the submarket was approximately 5.8%, representing a slight increase from the cyclical low of 4.3% observed in the first quarter of 2023 but still indicative of healthy market fundamentals. The average asking rent for Class A units in the submarket was approximately \$2,185 per month, reflecting an annualized rent growth rate of approximately 3.4% over the trailing twelve-month period. New supply has been moderate, with approximately 680 units delivered in 2023 and an estimated 520 units projected for delivery in 2024.

**[Comparable Rental Properties]{.underline}**

The appraiser identified and analyzed the following four properties as primary rental comparables for the subject:

**Comparable 1: The Bellweather at American Tobacco** --- Located at 318 Blackwell Street, approximately 0.4 miles south of the subject. This 186-unit Class A apartment community was completed in 2021 and features a unit mix of studios, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom units with a full amenity package including a rooftop pool and fitness center. As of the date of analysis, the property reported an average asking rent of \$2,310 per month and an occupancy rate of 96.2%.

**Comparable 2: Warehouse Lofts on Rigsbee** --- Located at 205 North Rigsbee Avenue, approximately 0.6 miles west of the subject. This 142-unit Class A adaptive reuse project was completed in 2020, featuring loft-style units with exposed brick and heavy timber construction. Average asking rent was \$2,175 per month with an occupancy rate of 94.8%. The slightly lower rent and occupancy levels relative to other comparables are attributed to the property\'s more limited amenity package and older vintage relative to the newest deliveries.

**Comparable 3: District on Main** --- Located at 411 West Main Street, approximately 0.3 miles southwest of the subject. This 224-unit Class A apartment community was completed in 2022 and is situated in the heart of the West Village district. The property features ground-floor retail, structured parking, and an extensive amenity package. Average asking rent was \$2,245 per month with an occupancy rate of 95.5%.

**Comparable 4: Foster Street Station** --- Located at 515 Foster Street, approximately 0.2 miles north of the subject. This 108-unit Class A development was completed in 2019 and represents the closest comparable to the subject in terms of immediate location. The property reported an average asking rent of \$2,095 per month and an occupancy rate of 97.1%. The lower average rent reflects the property\'s smaller unit sizes and the absence of premium amenities such as a rooftop terrace and pool.

**[Projected Rent Levels for Subject]{.underline}**

Based on the comparable rental analysis, the appraiser projects the following stabilized rent levels for the subject property:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Unit Type**           **Projected Rent Range**   **Projected Average Rent**
  ----------------------- -------------------------- ----------------------------
  One-Bedroom             \$2,100 -- \$2,350/month   \$2,175/month

  Two-Bedroom             \$2,450 -- \$2,750/month   \$2,550/month

  Three-Bedroom           \$2,950 -- \$3,200/month   \$3,050/month
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The weighted average monthly rent across all 212 units, incorporating the unit mix and projected rents, is approximately \$2,245 per month. These projections reflect the subject\'s advantages as a newly constructed Class A product with a superior amenity package and prime Brightleaf district location.

**[Retail Market]{.underline}**

The downtown Durham retail market continues to benefit from the increasing residential density and foot traffic generated by the neighborhood\'s multifamily and mixed-use developments. As of the third quarter of 2024, retail vacancy in the downtown core was approximately 4.2%, and triple-net rents for ground-floor retail space in comparable mixed-use projects ranged from \$26.00 to \$34.00 per square foot on a triple-net basis. The appraiser projects a stabilized retail rent of \$30.00 per square foot NNN for the subject\'s 18,400 square feet of ground-floor retail space, reflecting the property\'s excellent visibility, street-level access, and location within the active Brightleaf district.

**[Absorption Projection]{.underline}**

Based on historical absorption rates observed at the comparable properties during their initial lease-up periods, the appraiser estimates that the subject will achieve stabilized occupancy (defined as 95%) within approximately eight to ten months following receipt of the certificate of occupancy. The projected absorption rate is approximately 22 to 25 units per month, consistent with the pace observed at The Bellweather at American Tobacco (24 units per month) and District on Main (23 units per month) during their respective lease-up periods.

**[Demand Drivers]{.underline}**

Primary demand drivers for the subject property include Duke University and the Duke University Health System (the largest private employer in Durham), Research Triangle Park (located approximately 10 miles southeast), the downtown Durham employment corridor, and proximity to significant cultural and entertainment venues including the Durham Bulls Athletic Park, the Durham Performing Arts Center, and the American Tobacco Campus. Additionally, the growing presence of technology firms and startups in the downtown Durham area continues to attract a young, professionally employed renter demographic that represents the target market for the subject property.

**[Section 5 --- Highest and Best Use Analysis]{.underline}**

**[As Vacant]{.underline}**

The highest and best use of the subject property, as if vacant and available for development, was analyzed in accordance with the four standard tests: legal permissibility, physical possibility, financial feasibility, and maximum productivity. The site\'s MU-D zoning permits a range of uses including residential, retail, office, hotel, and mixed-use development, all by right, with structures up to 120 feet in height. The site\'s physical characteristics --- including its 3.47-acre size, generally level topography, availability of all municipal utilities, and favorable street frontage --- support a variety of development programs. Alternative uses considered in the analysis included office development, hotel development, and exclusively retail development. Each alternative was evaluated against a mixed-use residential and retail program. Based on the land residual analysis performed in the full appraisal report, a mixed-use residential and retail development of the type and scale proposed for the subject was determined to produce the highest land residual value and is therefore concluded to represent the highest and best use of the land as if vacant.

**[As Proposed (Improved)]{.underline}**

The highest and best use of the property as proposed --- that is, assuming construction of the 212-unit mixed-use residential and retail development as described in Section 3 --- satisfies all four tests. The proposed development is legally permissible under MU-D zoning without the need for variances or special permits. It is physically possible given the site\'s dimensions, topography, and infrastructure availability. It is financially feasible based on the income projections and cost analysis set forth in this report, which indicate that the prospective stabilized net operating income will support a market value in excess of the total development cost. Finally, the proposed development is maximally productive relative to alternative development programs analyzed by the appraiser, as it generates the highest return on cost among the programs considered.

**[Conclusion]{.underline}**

The proposed development of The Piedmont at Brightleaf --- a 212-unit Class A mixed-use residential and retail project --- represents the highest and best use of the subject property, both as if vacant and as proposed.

**[Section 6 --- Valuation Methodology and Conclusions]{.underline}**

**[Section 6.1 --- As-Is Land Valuation]{.underline}**

**Approach:** The as-is market value of the subject land was estimated using the sales comparison approach, which is the most reliable and widely accepted methodology for valuing vacant land in an active market with sufficient comparable data. The subject is valued in its current condition as of the effective date: vacant, cleared, and rough-graded, with environmental remediation completed and all municipal utilities available.

**Comparable Land Sales:** The appraiser identified and analyzed four recent sales of comparable development land in the downtown Durham and adjacent urban submarkets. Each comparable was adjusted for differences in location, size, shape, access, utilities, topography, and market conditions (time of sale). The comparable sales and adjustments are summarized below:

**Sale 1:** A 2.81-acre parcel located on West Chapel Hill Street, Durham, sold in July 2024 for \$7,447,000, or \$2,650,000 per acre. The parcel is zoned for mixed-use development and is located approximately 0.5 miles west of the subject. After adjustment for the subject\'s superior street frontage and slightly less favorable vehicular access from a secondary roadway, the adjusted rate is \$2,510,000 per acre.

**Sale 2:** A 1.95-acre parcel located on Morris Street, Durham, sold in April 2024 for \$5,460,000, or \$2,800,000 per acre. The parcel is smaller than the subject and has a more regular shape, which typically commands a premium on a per-acre basis for efficient development. After adjustment for the subject\'s larger size and irregular configuration, the adjusted rate is \$2,620,000 per acre.

**Sale 3:** A 4.12-acre parcel located on Mangum Street, Durham, sold in January 2024 for \$9,888,000, or \$2,400,000 per acre. The parcel is located in a transitional area approximately 0.7 miles north of the downtown core and was adjusted upward for the subject\'s superior Brightleaf district location and proximity to established amenities. The adjusted rate is \$2,550,000 per acre.

**Sale 4:** A 3.05-acre assemblage of two parcels located on Corporation Street, Durham, sold in September 2023 for \$7,168,000, or \$2,350,000 per acre. The sale occurred approximately 14 months prior to the effective date and was adjusted upward for market conditions (positive price trend in downtown Durham land values) and for the subject\'s superior frontage and access. The adjusted rate is \$2,480,000 per acre.

**Indicated Value Range:** The adjusted comparable sales indicate a range of \$2,480,000 to \$2,620,000 per acre for the subject land.

**Selected Rate:** After reconciliation of the comparable data, placing greatest weight on Sales 1 and 3 as most similar in size and location to the subject, the appraiser selected a rate of approximately \$2,565,000 per acre.

**As-Is Land Value:** 3.47 acres × \$2,565,000 per acre = \$8,900,550, rounded to **\$8,900,000**.

**Reconciliation:** The concluded as-is land value of \$8,900,000 is consistent with the land acquisition cost of \$8,200,000, which was the price paid by Harborview Capital Partners LLC in early 2024 prior to the demolition of the existing warehouse structures and the completion of environmental remediation. The demolition and remediation activities, which cost approximately \$680,000, have contributed to the current enhanced value of the land in its cleared and development-ready condition.

**[Section 6.2 --- As-Completed Valuation]{.underline}**

**Approaches Used:** The as-completed market value of the subject property was estimated using the income capitalization approach as the primary valuation methodology, supported by the sales comparison approach as a secondary check on reasonableness.

**Income Capitalization Approach**

The \"as-completed\" value reflects the market value of the proposed development upon completion of construction but prior to the achievement of stabilized occupancy. This valuation scenario recognizes that, at the point of construction completion, the property will not yet have reached its projected stabilized occupancy of 95% and the owner will incur costs and experience income loss during the lease-up period. Accordingly, the as-completed value is derived by deducting from the as-stabilized value the estimated costs and economic impact of the lease-up period.

The prospective stabilized net operating income (\"NOI\") of the subject, as detailed in Section 7 below, is \$4,876,800 per annum. Applied at the selected capitalization rate of 6.40%, the indicated as-stabilized value is \$76,200,000 (see Section 6.3 below).

**Lease-Up Deductions from As-Stabilized Value:**

The appraiser estimated the following deductions to account for the lease-up period between construction completion and stabilization:

> • **Estimated lease-up period:** 9 months (midpoint of the 8- to 10-month range projected in Section 4), commencing upon receipt of the certificate of occupancy.
>
> • **Lost rental income during lease-up:** Assuming a linear absorption from 0% to 95% occupancy over the 9-month period, the effective average occupancy during lease-up is approximately 47.5%. The resulting lost rental income relative to stabilized occupancy (95%) is estimated at approximately \$2,450,000.
>
> • **Lease-up costs:** Additional marketing expenditures, concessions to early tenants (estimated at an average of one month\'s free rent per unit), and supplemental on-site leasing staff are estimated to total approximately \$680,000.
>
> • **Total lease-up adjustment:** Approximately \$3,130,000.
>
> • **Discount for lease-up risk and timing:** An additional deduction of approximately \$270,000 is applied to account for the risk and present-value discount associated with the timing uncertainty of the lease-up period.
>
> • **Total deduction from as-stabilized value:** \$3,130,000 + \$270,000 = \$3,400,000.

**As-Completed Value via Income Approach:** \$76,200,000 − \$3,400,000 = **\$72,800,000**.

**Sales Comparison Approach (Supportive)**

As a supportive check on the income capitalization approach, the appraiser analyzed three comparable sales of recently constructed mixed-use multifamily properties in the Research Triangle area. The sales indicated a price range of \$330,000 to \$360,000 per residential unit, after adjustment for the retail component. Applied to the subject\'s 212 residential units, the midpoint of approximately \$343,000 per unit indicates a value of approximately \$72,700,000, which is highly supportive of the income approach conclusion.

**Concluded As-Completed Market Value: \$72,800,000**

**[Section 6.3 --- As-Stabilized Valuation]{.underline}**

**Approach:** The as-stabilized market value was estimated using the income capitalization approach, specifically the direct capitalization method.

**Stabilization Assumption:** Stabilized occupancy is defined as 95% across all residential units and retail bays, consistent with the observed stabilized occupancy levels at the comparable properties in the downtown Durham submarket.

**Projected Stabilization Date:** The appraiser projects that the subject will achieve stabilized occupancy approximately nine months following projected substantial completion, or approximately May 2028.

**Capitalization Rate Analysis:** The overall capitalization rate was derived from an analysis of five comparable property sales in the Raleigh-Durham metropolitan market, all involving Class A multifamily or mixed-use residential properties with recent construction dates. The observed capitalization rates for these transactions ranged from 5.75% to 7.10%, with a mean of approximately 6.35% and a median of approximately 6.40%. The variance in observed rates reflects differences in property quality, location, tenant profile, and the proportion of retail versus residential income.

**Selected Capitalization Rate: 6.40%.** The selected rate is positioned at the median of the comparable range and reflects the subject\'s status as a new-construction, Class A property in a prime downtown location with strong demand fundamentals. The rate also accounts for the current interest rate environment, which has stabilized following the tightening cycle of 2022-2023, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield trading at approximately 4.40% as of the effective date.

**Stabilized Net Operating Income:** \$4,876,800 per annum (as detailed in Section 7 below).

**As-Stabilized Value Calculation:**

\$4,876,800 ÷ 0.0640 = **\$76,200,000**

**Cross-Check:** The indicated as-stabilized value of \$76,200,000 implies a price per residential unit of approximately \$359,434 (\$76,200,000 ÷ 212 units). This metric falls within the range of \$340,000 to \$380,000 per unit observed for Class A new-construction multifamily properties in the downtown Durham submarket, confirming the reasonableness of the valuation conclusion. On a gross building area basis, the indicated value equates to approximately \$265.04 per square foot (\$76,200,000 ÷ 287,500 square feet), which is consistent with comparable market data.

**[Section 7 --- Projected Stabilized Income and Expense Analysis]{.underline}**

The following income and expense projections are based on the comparable rental data and operating expense analysis set forth in the full appraisal report. All projections assume stabilized occupancy at 95% and are presented on an annual basis.

**[Gross Potential Rental Income --- Residential]{.underline}**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Unit Type**          **Units**      **Average Monthly Rent**   **Annual Rent per Unit**   **Annual Gross Potential Rent**
  ---------------------- -------------- -------------------------- -------------------------- ---------------------------------
  One-Bedroom            142            \$2,175                    \$26,100                   \$3,706,200

  Two-Bedroom            56             \$2,550                    \$30,600                   \$1,713,600

  Three-Bedroom          14             \$3,050                    \$36,600                   \$512,400

  **Total / Subtotal**   **212**        ---                        ---                        **\$5,932,200**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The gross potential residential rent at face rents totals \$5,932,200, reflecting a weighted average monthly rent of approximately \$2,333 per unit. However, the appraiser has also performed a blended analysis incorporating market concessions (estimated at approximately one-half month per unit on average at stabilization, reflecting the competitive environment for newly delivered units), rent premiums for specific unit features (including floor-level premiums for upper-floor units, view premiums for units with skyline or courtyard views, and upgraded finish package premiums), and adjustments for unit layout and orientation. This blended analysis produces a normalized annual residential income of **\$5,712,000**, which equates to a blended effective average rent of approximately \$2,245 per month across all 212 units. The normalized figure is used in the income analysis below.

**[Gross Potential Rental Income --- Retail]{.underline}**

The subject\'s 18,400 square feet of ground-floor retail space is projected to generate gross potential rental income of **\$552,000** per annum, based on the concluded market rent of \$30.00 per square foot on a triple-net basis (18,400 SF × \$30.00/SF NNN = \$552,000). Under the triple-net retail lease structure, tenants are responsible for their pro rata share of property taxes, insurance, and common area maintenance expenses attributable to the retail space.

**[Other Income]{.underline}**

Additional income sources include:

  **Total Other Income**                                                     **\$198,000**
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ---------------------------------------- -----------------------------------

  Retail Rental Income                     \$552,000

  Other Income                             \$198,000

  **Gross Potential Income (GPI)**         **\$6,462,000**
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

**[Vacancy and Credit Loss]{.underline}**

A vacancy and credit loss allowance of 5.0% of gross potential income has been applied, reflecting the current submarket vacancy of approximately 5.8% adjusted for the subject\'s anticipated competitive advantages as a newly constructed, fully amenitized Class A property. The 5.0% rate is consistent with the stabilized vacancy levels observed at the comparable properties (ranging from 2.9% to 5.2%) and accounts for both physical vacancy and credit loss.

**Vacancy and Credit Loss:** \$6,462,000 × 5.0% = **(\$323,100)**

**[Effective Gross Income]{.underline}**

**Effective Gross Income (EGI):** \$6,462,000 − \$323,100 = **\$6,138,900**

The total operating expense ratio is \$1,262,100 ÷ \$6,138,900 = approximately 20.6% of effective gross income. This ratio is consistent with industry norms for new-construction Class A multifamily properties, which typically operate at expense ratios between 18% and 25% of EGI, depending on location, property management structure, and amenity level.

**[Net Operating Income]{.underline}**

**Net Operating Income (NOI):** \$6,138,900 − \$1,262,100 = **\$4,876,800**

The projected stabilized NOI of \$4,876,800 serves as the basis for both the as-stabilized valuation (Section 6.3) and the as-completed valuation (Section 6.2).

**[Section 8 --- Environmental Considerations]{.underline}**

The appraiser reviewed the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\") prepared by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC, dated October 28, 2024. The Phase I ESA was prepared by the firm\'s lead environmental consultant, Dr. James Whitfield, P.E., in general conformance with ASTM Standard Practice E 1527-21 for Environmental Site Assessments. The Phase I ESA encompassed both parcels comprising the subject property.

The Phase I ESA identified one Recognized Environmental Condition (\"REC\") affecting the subject property: residual petroleum contamination associated with a former underground storage tank (\"UST\") located on the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 (615 Foster Street). Historical records indicate that the UST was originally installed in the 1950s in connection with the former tobacco warehouse operations and was used for the storage of heating oil. The UST had not been in active use since approximately 1988.

A Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase II ESA\") was subsequently conducted in August 2024, also by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC. The Phase II ESA included the advancement of soil borings and the collection and laboratory analysis of soil and groundwater samples from the area surrounding the former UST location. The results of the Phase II ESA revealed petroleum hydrocarbon contamination levels in soil that exceeded the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (\"NCDEQ\") Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch (\"IHSB\") residential soil screening levels for certain constituents, including benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes (\"BTEX\"). However, the detected concentrations were below the applicable NCDEQ non-residential (commercial/industrial) soil screening levels.

Environmental remediation of the affected area was completed in September 2024. Remediation activities included the removal and proper disposal of the former UST, excavation and off-site disposal of approximately 320 cubic yards of petroleum-impacted soil, and post-remediation confirmation sampling. The remediation was performed under the oversight of NCDEQ and in accordance with an approved remediation work plan.

Following completion of the remediation, NCDEQ issued a No Further Action (\"NFA\") letter dated September 30, 2024, for the affected area. The NFA letter confirms that no further investigation or remediation is required, subject to the following conditions:

> \(i\) A soil vapor mitigation system must be installed and maintained in the structured parking garage and any enclosed occupied space constructed above the affected area, in accordance with specifications approved by NCDEQ; and
>
> \(ii\) Future use of the affected portion of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 --- specifically, an area encompassing approximately 0.38 acres in the northeast corner of the parcel --- is restricted to non-residential purposes. This land use restriction is memorialized in a Declaration of Land Use Restrictions recorded at the Durham County Register of Deeds.

The appraiser notes that the soil vapor mitigation system required by the NFA letter has been incorporated into the construction plans and specifications prepared by Meridian Design Collective PC and is included within the GMP contract with Graystone Construction Group Inc. The cost of the vapor mitigation system is reflected in the hard construction cost budget.

The NFA letter restricts future use of the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 (approximately 0.38 acres) to non-residential use. The appraiser notes this restriction for the record. The project plans, as reviewed by the appraiser and as described by the developer, include residential units on the upper floors of the building positioned above this area of the site. The appraiser\'s valuation assumes that the borrower will comply with all applicable environmental laws, regulations, and use restrictions, and that any required modifications, variances, or additional remediation necessary to permit the planned use will be obtained by the borrower at the borrower\'s cost. The appraiser expresses no opinion as to the legal permissibility of the planned residential use of the area above the environmentally restricted portion of the site. The appraiser has not adjusted the valuation conclusions to account for any potential impact of the NFA use restriction on the residential unit mix or leasability of units positioned above the restricted area.

The appraiser is not an environmental consultant and does not render opinions regarding environmental conditions, remediation adequacy, or compliance with environmental regulations. The reader is directed to the Phase I and Phase II ESA reports prepared by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC for a complete discussion of environmental matters.

**[1. Executive Summary of Findings]{.underline}**

Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC (\"Sentinel\") was retained by Harborview Capital Partners LLC (\"Harborview\" or \"Client\") to conduct a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\" or \"Assessment\") of the property located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701 (the \"Subject Property\"). The assessment was conducted for the purpose of supporting proposed financing by Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. (\"Pinnacle\" or \"Lender\") and to satisfy the requirements of the All Appropriate Inquiries (\"AAI\") rule under 40 C.F.R. Part 312, thereby supporting potential assertion of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (\"CERCLA\") innocent landowner, contiguous property owner, and bona fide prospective purchaser defenses.

The Subject Property consists of two contiguous parcels: Parcel ID 0821-04-72-3341 (approximately 1.89 acres, fronting 601 Foster Street) and Parcel ID 0821-04-72-4102 (approximately 1.58 acres, fronting 615 Foster Street), totaling approximately 3.47 acres of land. The Subject Property is situated within Durham\'s historic Brightleaf tobacco district, an area that has experienced significant redevelopment over the past two decades. The property is currently vacant improved land. Former tobacco warehouse structures that had occupied both parcels were demolished in August 2024, and environmental remediation activities were completed in September 2024. The site is graded and secured with temporary construction fencing.

The property is zoned MU-D (Mixed Use --- Downtown) by the City of Durham and is planned for development as \"The Piedmont at Brightleaf,\" a 212-unit Class A mixed-use residential and retail development. The proposed project includes 18,400 square feet of ground-floor retail space and a 276-space structured parking garage. The building is designed as a 6-story structure --- five residential levels over one podium level --- with a total gross building area of approximately 287,500 square feet. The project architect is Meridian Design Collective PC, and the general contractor is Graystone Construction Group Inc. (NC License No. 78442).

Based on the assessment conducted herein, one Recognized Environmental Condition (\"REC\") was identified at the Subject Property. The REC consists of residual petroleum contamination from a former underground storage tank (\"UST\") located in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. The former UST, a 2,000-gallon diesel fuel tank, was historically associated with a backup generator that served the tobacco warehouse operations. The REC has been subject to a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment investigation (August 2024) and subsequent remediation consisting of soil excavation and off-site disposal (September 2024). A No Further Action (\"NFA\") determination letter was issued by the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (\"NCDEQ\"), Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch (\"IHSB\"), on September 30, 2024, for Site ID IHSB-24-1203.

The NFA letter is conditional. It is premised upon (a) the installation of a soil vapor mitigation system beneath any enclosed structure constructed over the affected area, (b) a restriction of future use to non-residential purposes on the affected approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, (c) compliance with a soil management plan for future excavation activities within the affected area, and (d) the recording of a deed notice in the Durham County Registry of Deeds within 60 days of the NFA letter date.

No other Recognized Environmental Conditions, Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"CRECs\"), or Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"HRECs\") were identified during this assessment. Several de minimis conditions were noted during the site reconnaissance and are described in the full report; however, these conditions do not rise to the level of RECs under ASTM E1527-21.

**[2. Site Description and History]{.underline}**

**2.1 Physical Description**

The Subject Property is composed of two contiguous parcels at 601 Foster Street (Parcel 0821-04-72-3341, approximately 1.89 acres) and 615 Foster Street (Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, approximately 1.58 acres), located in downtown Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701. The combined area of the two parcels is approximately 3.47 acres. The site fronts Foster Street to the north and is bounded by commercial and mixed-use properties on the remaining sides.

The topography of the Subject Property is generally flat, with a gentle slope of approximately 2 percent from northwest to southeast. Site elevation ranges from approximately 395 feet to 401 feet above mean sea level, as confirmed by topographic survey and regional United States Geological Survey data. The site drains generally toward the southeast, consistent with the surrounding topographic gradient and the regional drainage pattern toward the Ellerbe Creek watershed.

The site is currently vacant. All former structures have been demolished and removed as of August 2024. The ground surface has been graded and the site is enclosed by temporary six-foot chain-link construction fencing with green privacy screening. Existing utility infrastructure --- including municipal water and sanitary sewer lines, electrical service, natural gas, and telecommunications conduit --- has been stubbed to the property boundaries in anticipation of the proposed development. A 20-foot utility easement runs along the western boundary of the site and is occupied by Duke Energy utility poles and overhead electrical lines. A stormwater management easement of approximately 0.22 acres, recorded in the Durham County Registry of Deeds at Book 7421, Page 212, occupies the southern portion of the site and contains a graded drainage swale and inlet structure.

**2.2 Historical Use Summary**

The historical use of the Subject Property was researched through review of Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps (1901, 1913, 1924, 1937, 1950), historical aerial photographs (1955, 1965, 1972, 1981, 1993, 2005, 2012, 2019), city directories (various years, 1910--2005), Durham County building permit records, Durham County tax records, and interviews with persons knowledgeable about the property. The following chronological summary was developed from these sources:

**1900--1965:** Both parcels were occupied by tobacco warehouses and associated processing buildings. The site was part of Durham\'s historic Brightleaf tobacco district, which was the center of the American bright-leaf tobacco industry during the early twentieth century. Sanborn maps from 1901 through 1950 depict large, multi-bay warehouse structures on both parcels, with rail siding access along the southern boundary of the property. The warehouses were used for the curing, grading, and storage of leaf tobacco, and later for the manufacture of tobacco products. These operations were consistent with the industrial character of the surrounding area during this period.

**1965--1990:** Following the decline of the Durham tobacco industry, the warehouse buildings were converted to light industrial and general commercial storage uses. City directory listings from this period indicate tenants including a furniture refinishing operation, a printing company, and a general storage and distribution business. During this period, a 2,000-gallon underground storage tank was installed on the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 to store diesel fuel for a backup generator serving the warehouse operations. Based on a review of Durham County building permit records, the estimated installation date of the UST is approximately 1972. The UST was reportedly decommissioned and removed in approximately 1998; however, no formal UST closure records were located in the files of the Durham County Fire Marshal or the NCDEQ UST Section despite Sentinel\'s diligent efforts to obtain such records.

**1990--2005:** Light industrial use continued at diminishing levels. Several tenants vacated the property during the 1990s, and by the early 2000s the warehouse buildings were largely unoccupied. Aerial photographs from 1993 and 2005 show the buildings in increasingly deteriorated condition, with portions of the roofing compromised and vegetation encroaching on the southern portions of the site. Surface parking occupied portions of the unpaved areas between the buildings during this period.

**2005--2022:** The property was largely vacant, with the warehouse structures remaining in place but unoccupied. The site was used intermittently as unpaved surface parking, primarily serving visitors to the adjacent Brightleaf Historic District and American Tobacco Campus. Ownership of the parcels changed multiple times during this period, as reflected in the Durham County deed records.

**2022--Present:** Harborview Capital Partners LLC acquired the Subject Property in 2022 for the purpose of redevelopment. A pre-demolition hazardous materials survey was conducted by an independent consultant in July 2024, and demolition of the remaining warehouse structures was completed in August 2024. Environmental remediation, consisting of excavation and off-site disposal of petroleum-impacted soil in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, was completed in September 2024.

**2.3 Surrounding Land Uses and Environmental Setting**

The Subject Property is situated in a mixed commercial and entertainment district in downtown Durham. Surrounding land uses include the Brightleaf Historic District (commercial retail and restaurant uses) to the north and west, the American Tobacco Campus (mixed-use commercial, office, and entertainment development) to the south, and the Durham Performing Arts Center and associated commercial development to the east. These surrounding properties are generally developed with commercial or institutional uses and do not present obvious indicators of significant environmental concern with respect to the Subject Property.

The site is located in the Durham Triassic Basin, a geological formation characterized by interbedded sandstone, siltstone, and mudstone of the Newark Supergroup. Depth to groundwater in the vicinity of the Subject Property is estimated at approximately 15 to 25 feet below grade, based on regional hydrogeological data and measurements obtained from monitoring wells installed during the Phase II investigation. The inferred groundwater flow direction is generally to the southeast, consistent with the regional topographic gradient.

The Subject Property is not located within a Federal Emergency Management Agency (\"FEMA\") designated Special Flood Hazard Area. According to FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map Panel 3720098700J, effective March 2, 2009, the site is located in Zone X, an area of minimal flood hazard.

**[3. Environmental Database and Regulatory Records Review]{.underline}**

A standard ASTM-required environmental database search was conducted by Environmental Data Resources, Inc. (\"EDR\") for the Subject Property and surrounding areas within the applicable ASTM search radii. The database search date was October 10, 2024, and the complete search report is attached as Appendix A to the full Phase I ESA report.

**3.1 Subject Property Listings**

The Subject Property was identified in the following regulatory databases:

**NCDEQ Incident Management Database (IMD):** The property at 615 Foster Street (Parcel 0821-04-72-4102) is listed as Site No. NONUST-24-0847 in the NCDEQ Incident Management Database. This listing relates to the petroleum contamination identified during the Phase II investigation conducted in August 2024 in connection with the former 2,000-gallon diesel UST. The incident was reported to NCDEQ on August 12, 2024, following the confirmation of contamination above applicable soil remediation goals.

**NCDEQ Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch Database:** The Subject Property is listed as Site ID IHSB-24-1203 in the NCDEQ IHSB database. The current status of this listing is \"NFA --- Conditional\" as of September 30, 2024, reflecting the issuance of the conditional No Further Action determination letter described in Section 7 of this report.

The Subject Property was not identified on the National Priorities List (\"NPL\"), the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Information System (\"CERCLIS\"), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Information System (\"RCRIS\") as either a large-quantity or small-quantity generator of hazardous waste, the North Carolina Pre-Regulatory Landfill Inventory, the North Carolina equivalent superfund list, or any other federal or state database that would indicate the presence of additional environmental conditions beyond those already identified herein.

**3.2 Adjoining and Nearby Property Listings**

The EDR database search identified several properties within the applicable ASTM search radii that are listed on various environmental databases. Specifically, three nearby properties are listed as active Leaking Underground Storage Tank (\"LUST\") sites within the one-half mile ASTM search radius. Upon review, these LUST sites are located either cross-gradient or down-gradient of the Subject Property relative to the inferred groundwater flow direction. Based on the distance from the Subject Property, the reported nature and extent of contamination at these off-site locations, and the groundwater flow direction, Sentinel concluded that these nearby LUST sites do not represent RECs for the Subject Property and would not be expected to have impacted the Subject Property\'s subsurface conditions.

No other nearby or adjoining property listings were identified that would be expected to have adversely affected the environmental conditions at the Subject Property.

**3.3 UST Records**

No active underground storage tanks are registered for the Subject Property in the NCDEQ UST database. Historical records, including building permit files and Sanborn map annotations, indicate that a 2,000-gallon diesel UST was present on the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 from approximately 1972 to approximately 1998. Despite Sentinel\'s attempts to obtain formal UST closure documentation from both the Durham County Fire Marshal\'s office and the NCDEQ UST Section, no closure records were located. The absence of closure records is noted as a data gap, although the Phase II investigation and subsequent remediation have substantively addressed the environmental conditions associated with the former UST.

**3.4 NCDEQ File Review**

Sentinel reviewed the NCDEQ project files maintained at the NCDEQ Mooresville Regional Office pertaining to Site No. NONUST-24-0847 and Site ID IHSB-24-1203. The file contains the Phase II investigation report dated August 30, 2024, the remediation work plan and completion report dated September 25, 2024, post-remediation groundwater monitoring data, and the No Further Action letter dated September 30, 2024. The contents of these files are consistent with the information summarized in this report and in the full Phase I ESA.

**[4. Site Reconnaissance Observations]{.underline}**

A site reconnaissance was conducted on October 15, 2024, by Dr. James Whitfield, P.E., Senior Principal Environmental Scientist, and Sarah Ng, Environmental Scientist, both of Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC. **[5. Phase II Investigation Results (Summary)]{.underline}**

*Note: The Phase II Environmental Site Assessment referenced in this section was performed by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC under a separate scope of work and separate contractual engagement in August 2024. The Phase I ESA does not include sampling or analysis as part of its scope. The following summary is provided for reference and completeness in understanding the environmental conditions identified at the Subject Property. The complete Phase II investigation report is available under separate cover (Sentinel Project No. SEC-2024-1089) and is also referenced in the NCDEQ project files for Site ID IHSB-24-1203.*

**5.1 Scope of Investigation**

The Phase II investigation was conducted in August 2024 and was focused on the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, in the vicinity of the former 2,000-gallon diesel underground storage tank. The investigation scope included the advancement of twelve soil borings (designated SB-01 through SB-12) to depths ranging from 15 to 25 feet below grade, the installation and sampling of three groundwater monitoring wells (designated MW-01, MW-02, and MW-03), and the collection of soil gas samples from eight sub-slab soil gas probes (designated SG-01 through SG-08) installed at a depth of approximately 5 feet below grade. All sampling and analysis were conducted in accordance with NCDEQ-approved sampling protocols, and all samples were analyzed by a North Carolina-certified analytical laboratory (Pace Analytical Services, Huntersville, North Carolina).

**5.2 Soil Analytical Results**

Total petroleum hydrocarbons in the diesel range organics (\"TPH-DRO\") fraction were detected in soil samples collected from borings within and adjacent to the former UST location at concentrations ranging from non-detect (below the laboratory method detection limit of 5.0 mg/kg) to a maximum of 847 mg/kg in soil boring SB-07 at a depth of 10 feet below grade. Benzene was detected in soil samples at a maximum concentration of 0.42 mg/kg, also in boring SB-07 at a depth of 8 feet below grade. Additional petroleum-related constituents, including toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes, were detected at lower concentrations in several borings within the affected area.

The lateral extent of petroleum contamination was generally limited to an area of approximately 0.38 acres in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. Borings SB-05 through SB-09, located within this area, exhibited the highest concentrations, while borings SB-01 through SB-04, SB-10, SB-11, and SB-12, located outside or at the periphery of the affected area, exhibited non-detect or trace-level concentrations. Vertically, the contamination extended from approximately 4 feet to 14 feet below grade, with the highest concentrations observed at depths of 8 to 12 feet, consistent with the inferred depth of the former UST and the surrounding backfill soils.

The detected concentrations were compared to the NCDEQ Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch Preliminary Soil Remediation Goals (\"PSRGs\") for both residential and non-residential land uses. The following table summarizes the critical comparisons:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Constituent**   **Maximum Detected Concentration**   **NCDEQ Residential PSRG**   **Exceeds Residential?**   **NCDEQ Non-Residential PSRG**   **Exceeds Non-Residential?**
  ----------------- ------------------------------------ ---------------------------- -------------------------- -------------------------------- ------------------------------
  TPH-DRO           847 mg/kg                            100 mg/kg                    Yes                        1,000 mg/kg                      No

  Benzene           0.42 mg/kg                           0.065 mg/kg                  Yes                        0.89 mg/kg                       No
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As indicated in the table above, the maximum detected concentrations of both TPH-DRO and benzene in soil exceeded the NCDEQ residential PSRGs but were below the NCDEQ non-residential (commercial/industrial) PSRGs. This distinction is significant because the NCDEQ applies different risk-based cleanup standards depending on the intended land use. The residential PSRGs are more stringent because they are designed to be protective of long-term residential exposure, including exposure to young children and other sensitive populations, under a 30-year residential exposure scenario.

**5.3 Groundwater Analytical Results**

Dissolved-phase petroleum constituents were detected in groundwater samples collected from monitoring well MW-02, which is located within the affected area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. Specifically, dissolved benzene was detected at a concentration of 0.8 µg/L (the North Carolina 2L Groundwater Quality Standard for benzene is 1.0 µg/L) and dissolved TPH-DRO was detected at 320 µg/L. All other dissolved-phase constituents were either non-detect or detected at concentrations well below applicable 2L Standards. Monitoring wells MW-01 and MW-03, located on the periphery of the affected area, did not exhibit detectable concentrations of dissolved petroleum constituents, indicating that the dissolved-phase groundwater plume has not migrated significantly beyond the immediate vicinity of the former UST location and does not appear to have migrated off-site.

**5.4 Soil Gas Analytical Results**

Volatile organic compounds, including benzene and naphthalene, were detected in soil gas samples collected from probes within and near the affected area. The most significant soil gas detection was benzene at a concentration of 185 µg/m³ in soil gas sample SG-04, which is located within the center of the affected area. The NCDEQ residential vapor intrusion screening level for benzene in sub-slab soil gas is 31 µg/m³. The detected concentration of 185 µg/m³ exceeds this screening level by a factor of approximately six, indicating the potential for vapor intrusion into enclosed structures constructed over the affected area. Naphthalene was also detected in soil gas samples SG-03, SG-04, and SG-05 at concentrations ranging from 22 to 89 µg/m³.

These soil gas results support the conclusion that a soil vapor mitigation system will be required beneath any enclosed structure constructed over the affected area to prevent the migration of volatile petroleum constituents into indoor air at concentrations that could pose a risk to building occupants.

**[6. Remediation Summary]{.underline}**

Following the completion of the Phase II investigation and confirmation that soil contamination in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 exceeded NCDEQ residential PSRGs, Harborview Capital Partners LLC retained Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC to conduct remediation of the identified petroleum contamination. Remediation activities were performed in September 2024 in accordance with a remediation work plan approved by the NCDEQ Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch.

**6.1 Scope of Remediation**

The primary remediation activity consisted of the excavation and off-site disposal of petroleum-impacted soil from the affected area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. Approximately 1,200 cubic yards of soil were excavated from the affected area, with excavation depths reaching approximately 12 feet below grade in the most heavily impacted zone (corresponding to the area surrounding soil borings SB-06 and SB-07). The excavation was conducted using conventional earthmoving equipment under the oversight of Sentinel field personnel, with continuous air monitoring conducted at the excavation perimeter to ensure worker and community safety.

Confirmation soil samples were collected from the excavation sidewalls and base at the completion of excavation activities. The confirmation sampling results demonstrated that residual contamination remains in situ at concentrations below the NCDEQ non-residential PSRGs throughout the excavation area. However, residual contamination remains above the NCDEQ residential PSRGs in certain areas at depths of 10 to 14 feet below grade, particularly along the eastern property boundary where excavation was limited by the proximity of the adjoining property and critical underground utility infrastructure (a 12-inch sanitary sewer main and associated service laterals). Complete removal of all contamination exceeding residential standards was not feasible without risk of damage to the adjacent underground utilities and potential encroachment onto the adjoining property.

All impacted soil removed during the excavation was transported under proper chain-of-custody documentation and disposed of at the Lee County Environmental Landfill, a permitted Subtitle D solid waste management facility located in Sanford, North Carolina. Waste characterization sampling confirmed that the impacted soil met the acceptance criteria for Subtitle D disposal and did not exhibit hazardous waste characteristics under 40 C.F.R. Part 261.

Groundwater encountered during excavation was managed in accordance with an NCDEQ-approved water management plan. Approximately 45,000 gallons of groundwater were pumped from the excavation, treated through granular activated carbon filtration, and discharged under a temporary NPDES general permit.

**6.2 Post-Remediation Monitoring**

Two rounds of post-remediation groundwater monitoring were conducted, on September 15 and October 1, 2024, respectively. Groundwater samples collected from monitoring wells MW-01, MW-02, and MW-03 exhibited decreasing concentrations of dissolved petroleum constituents. All dissolved-phase constituents were detected at concentrations below the applicable North Carolina 2L Groundwater Quality Standards in both monitoring rounds, indicating that the excavation remediation has effectively reduced the dissolved-phase groundwater contamination to below regulatory standards.

**6.3 Remediation Cost**

The total cost of the remediation activities, including excavation, soil disposal, water management, confirmation sampling, and post-remediation monitoring, was approximately \$485,000. This cost was funded by Harborview Capital Partners LLC.

**[7. NCDEQ No Further Action (NFA) Letter --- Summary of Conditions]{.underline}**

On September 30, 2024, the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality, Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch, issued a No Further Action (\"NFA\") determination letter for Site ID IHSB-24-1203 / Incident No. NONUST-24-0847 (the \"NFA Letter\"). The NFA Letter was addressed to Harborview Capital Partners LLC as the current property owner and responsible party. A complete copy of the NFA Letter is attached as Appendix E to the full Phase I ESA report. The following is a summary of the material terms and conditions of the NFA Letter.

The NFA Letter states that, based on a review of the Phase II investigation data, the remediation completion report, and the post-remediation groundwater monitoring results, NCDEQ has determined that no further remediation action is required at the Subject Property at this time. This determination is expressly conditioned upon compliance with the following requirements:

**Condition 1 --- Soil Vapor Mitigation System.** A soil vapor mitigation system must be installed beneath any enclosed structure constructed over the affected area, which is identified as the approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, as delineated in the Phase II investigation report and shown on Figure 3 of this report. The NFA Letter specifies that the system shall consist of a passive sub-slab depressurization system with the capability for conversion to an active depressurization system if subsequent monitoring indicates that passive ventilation is insufficient to maintain indoor air quality below applicable screening levels. The system must be designed by a licensed professional engineer registered in the State of North Carolina and must be installed in accordance with NCDEQ Division of Waste Management guidelines for vapor intrusion mitigation. As-built drawings and a system performance verification report must be submitted to NCDEQ within 90 days of the completion of the building foundation in the affected area.

**Condition 2 --- Land Use Restriction (Non-Residential).** The NFA determination is issued on the basis that the affected portion of the Subject Property --- the approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 --- will be restricted to non-residential use. The NFA Letter states, in relevant part:

> \"Residual soil contamination concentrations in the affected area exceed the NCDEQ Preliminary Soil Remediation Goals for residential land use. Accordingly, this No Further Action determination is contingent upon the restriction of future use of the affected area to non-residential (commercial or industrial) purposes. Any change in land use to residential or other sensitive use on the affected portion of the parcel would require additional investigation and/or remediation to demonstrate that such use is protective of human health and the environment, and a modification to this NFA determination would need to be obtained from NCDEQ prior to such change in use.\"

This non-residential use restriction is the central condition of the NFA Letter and has direct implications for the proposed development of the Subject Property, as discussed further in Sections 8 and 10 of this report.

**Condition 3 --- Soil Management Plan.** Any future excavation, grading, or soil disturbance within the affected area must be conducted in accordance with a NCDEQ-approved soil management plan to ensure proper identification, handling, and disposal of residual contaminated soil. The soil management plan must address procedures for soil screening, stockpile management, dust control, worker health and safety, and disposal of any excavated soil that exceeds applicable waste characterization thresholds. The NFA Letter requires that the soil management plan be submitted to and approved by NCDEQ prior to commencement of any construction activities involving subsurface disturbance within the affected area.

**Condition 4 --- Deed Notice.** The property owner is required to record a notice in the Durham County Registry of Deeds providing notice to future purchasers, lessees, and other parties of the residual contamination present within the affected area and the land use restriction applicable to the affected area. The NFA Letter requires this deed notice to be recorded within 60 days of the date of the NFA Letter --- that is, by November 29, 2024. The deed notice must include a description of the affected area by metes and bounds or by reference to a recorded plat, a description of the nature and extent of residual contamination, and a statement of the non-residential use restriction.

As of the date of this Phase I ESA (October 28, 2024), the consultant was not provided evidence that the required deed notice has been recorded. The 60-day recording deadline of November 29, 2024, had not yet passed as of the assessment date. The client should ensure timely recording of the deed notice to maintain compliance with the NFA conditions.

It is important to note that the NFA Letter does not constitute a \"clean closure\" or a determination that the Subject Property is free of all environmental contamination. The NFA Letter expressly acknowledges that residual petroleum contamination remains in the subsurface within the affected area at concentrations exceeding residential PSRGs. The NFA determination is site-specific and applies only to the conditions known at the time of its issuance. Changes in site conditions, regulatory standards, or land use that are inconsistent with the conditions of the NFA Letter could require reopening the regulatory file and additional investigation or remediation.

**[8. Findings and Identified Environmental Conditions]{.underline}**

Based on the research, investigation, site reconnaissance, and analysis conducted as part of this Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Sentinel has identified the following environmental conditions at the Subject Property in accordance with the classification framework established by ASTM Standard Practice E1527-21.

**8.1 Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs)**

**One REC was identified at the Subject Property:**

Residual petroleum contamination, consisting of total petroleum hydrocarbons --- diesel range organics (\"TPH-DRO\") and benzene, is present in soil and soil gas in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, in the area of a former 2,000-gallon diesel underground storage tank. The contamination affects an area of approximately 0.38 acres. Although remediation has been conducted and a conditional NFA letter has been issued by NCDEQ, the NFA is premised upon ongoing compliance with specified conditions, and residual contamination remains in place at concentrations exceeding the NCDEQ residential Preliminary Soil Remediation Goals for both TPH-DRO and benzene in soil. Volatile organic compounds in soil gas within the affected area also exceed NCDEQ residential vapor intrusion screening levels.

This condition constitutes a REC as defined in ASTM E1527-21, Section 3.2.84, because the presence of residual petroleum contamination above unrestricted use standards represents \"the presence or likely presence of any hazardous substances or petroleum products in, on, or at a property: (i) due to a release to the environment; (ii) under conditions indicative of a release to the environment; or (iii) under conditions that pose a material threat of a future release to the environment.\"

*Note regarding classification as REC versus CREC:* The consultant considered whether this condition should be classified as a Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (\"CREC\") rather than a REC. Under ASTM E1527-21, Section 3.2.25, a CREC is defined as \"a recognized environmental condition resulting from a past release of hazardous substances or petroleum products that has been addressed to the satisfaction of the applicable regulatory authority...with hazardous substances or petroleum products allowed to remain in place subject to the implementation of required controls.\" Given that NCDEQ has issued an NFA determination with conditions --- including the soil vapor mitigation requirement, land use restriction, soil management plan, and deed notice --- this condition possesses many characteristics of a CREC. However, as of the date of this assessment, the required deed notice had not yet been recorded in the Durham County Registry of Deeds, and the required soil vapor mitigation system had not yet been designed or installed. Because the NFA conditions have not been fully implemented, the consultant has classified this condition as a REC, representing a conservative and protective approach. Upon full implementation of all NFA conditions --- including recording of the deed notice, installation and verification of the vapor mitigation system, and submittal of the soil management plan --- this condition may be reclassified as a CREC in a future assessment update.

**8.2 Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (CRECs)**

No Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified at the Subject Property as of the date of this assessment. As noted above, the identified REC may be reclassified as a CREC in the future upon full implementation of all NCDEQ NFA conditions.

**8.3 Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs)**

No Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified at the Subject Property.

The following de minimis conditions were observed during the site reconnaissance and/or identified through the research conducted for this assessment. These conditions do not rise to the level of RECs under ASTM E1527-21 and are not considered to represent a material threat to human health or the environment:

The fill material appeared to consist of construction and demolition debris (brick fragments, concrete pieces) mixed with soil, likely associated with the recent demolition of the former warehouse structures. This material did not exhibit staining, odors, or other indicators of contamination.
