**8.5 Business Environmental Risks**

The conditional NFA land use restriction limiting the affected 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 to non-residential use may constitute a business environmental risk to the Client and its lender if the proposed development includes residential use of the affected area. Under ASTM E1527-21, business environmental risks are not required to be identified as part of the standard Phase I ESA scope; however, the consultant notes this potential risk as a matter of professional judgment and in the interest of the Client.

A review of the preliminary site plans provided by the Client (drawing set dated September 12, 2024, prepared by Meridian Design Collective PC) indicates that the proposed development includes a 6-story mixed-use building with a ground-level podium (parking garage and retail) and five levels of residential units on floors 2 through 6. The building footprint extends across substantial portions of both parcels. The consultant did not independently verify whether any residential units would be positioned directly above the affected 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, as this determination requires a detailed overlay of the proposed building floor plans with the environmental delineation map prepared as part of the Phase II investigation (see Figure 3 --- Site Map, Section 12 of this report). The Client and its design team should verify the spatial relationship between the affected area and any proposed residential occupancy spaces, and should consult with environmental counsel regarding the implications of the NFA land use restriction for the proposed development program.

**[10. Recommendations]{.underline}**

Based on the findings, identified environmental conditions, and conclusions set forth in this Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC offers the following recommendations to the Client and the Lender.

**Recommendation 1 --- Verify Spatial Relationship of Residential Units to Restricted Area.** The Client and its project architect (Meridian Design Collective PC) should verify whether any proposed residential units in The Piedmont at Brightleaf development will be positioned directly above the approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 that is subject to the NCDEQ non-residential use restriction under the NFA Letter. This verification should be accomplished by overlaying the proposed building floor plans (including unit layouts for floors 2 through 6) with the environmental delineation map prepared as part of the Phase II investigation (reproduced as Figure 3 in this report). If the overlay confirms that residential units are planned directly above the affected area, the Client should consult with qualified environmental legal counsel regarding the need to either (a) obtain a formal modification to the NFA determination from NCDEQ permitting residential use of the affected area, which would likely require additional environmental investigation, risk assessment, and potentially additional remediation to demonstrate that residential use is protective of human health and the environment under a 30-year residential exposure scenario, or (b) redesign the project to eliminate residential uses above the affected area, such as by repositioning the residential unit layout or converting the affected portion of the upper floors to non-residential uses (e.g., common areas, amenity spaces, or commercial uses). The cost and timeline implications of either approach should be carefully evaluated by the Client, its design team, and its lender.

**Recommendation 2 --- Soil Vapor Mitigation System Design and Installation.** The Client should engage a licensed professional engineer to design the required soil vapor mitigation system for any enclosed space --- including the structured parking garage and any ground-floor retail space --- constructed over the affected area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. The system should be designed as a passive sub-slab depressurization system with conversion capability to active depressurization, as specified in the NFA Letter. Design of the vapor mitigation system should commence during the construction design development phase to ensure that the system is fully integrated into the building foundation and structural plans. As-built drawings and a performance verification report must be submitted to NCDEQ within 90 days of the completion of the building foundation in the affected area, as required by the NFA Letter.

**Recommendation 3 --- Record Deed Notice.** The NFA Letter requires the recording of a deed notice in the Durham County Registry of Deeds within 60 days of September 30, 2024 --- that is, by November 29, 2024. The deed notice must describe the affected area, the nature of the residual contamination, and the non-residential use restriction. The Client should confirm that this deed notice has been or will be timely prepared, reviewed by legal counsel, and recorded. Failure to record the deed notice within the required timeframe could jeopardize the NFA status and may constitute non-compliance with the conditions of the NFA determination. The Client\'s environmental counsel should also review the form and content of the deed notice to ensure that it is consistent with the NFA Letter requirements and does not inadvertently create title encumbrances or restrictions beyond those required by NCDEQ.

**Recommendation 4 --- Soil Management Plan.** A soil management plan should be prepared and submitted to NCDEQ for review and approval prior to commencement of any excavation, grading, or other subsurface disturbance activities within the affected area. The soil management plan should address procedures for visual and olfactory screening of excavated soils, stockpile management, dust suppression, personal protective equipment requirements, worker health and safety protocols, and disposal of any excavated soil that exceeds waste characterization thresholds. All construction personnel working within or adjacent to the affected area should receive training on the potential for encountering contaminated soil and the procedures established in the soil management plan. The soil management plan should be incorporated into the construction specifications and made available to the general contractor (Graystone Construction Group Inc.) and all relevant subcontractors.

**Recommendation 5 --- Ongoing Indoor Air Quality and Soil Gas Monitoring.** The Client should consider voluntarily conducting periodic indoor air quality monitoring or sub-slab soil gas monitoring after construction of any enclosed spaces over the affected area to verify the continued effectiveness of the soil vapor mitigation system. While such monitoring is not expressly required by the NFA Letter, it would provide ongoing documentation that indoor air quality is maintained below applicable screening levels and would serve as an additional safeguard for building occupants. Monitoring should be conducted at a frequency and according to a protocol approved by a qualified environmental professional.

**Recommendation 6 --- Environmental Insurance.** The Client and the Lender (Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.) may wish to evaluate the merits of obtaining a pollution legal liability (\"PLL\") insurance policy to address potential environmental liability associated with the residual contamination at the Subject Property. A PLL policy could provide coverage for costs associated with, among other things, obtaining an NFA modification from NCDEQ, conducting additional remediation if required, defending against third-party claims related to the contamination, and responding to unknown environmental conditions that may be discovered during construction. The availability, terms, and cost of PLL coverage should be discussed with a qualified environmental insurance broker.

**Recommendation 7 --- Update Assessment Before Closing if Necessary.** If the loan closing for the proposed development occurs after April 26, 2025 (180 days from the date of this report), this Phase I ESA will need to be updated in accordance with 40 C.F.R. § 312.20(c) to maintain compliance with the All Appropriate Inquiries requirements. The Client\'s currently anticipated closing date of February 28, 2025, falls within the 180-day AAI compliance window. However, if the closing is delayed beyond April 26, 2025, the Client should contact Sentinel to arrange for an update to this assessment, which would typically include an updated site reconnaissance, a review of any new regulatory actions or database listings, and an updated assessment of environmental conditions. **[SECTION 1: ORGANIZATIONAL CHART --- HARBORVIEW CAPITAL PARTNERS LLC]{.underline}**

**[1.1 Borrower Entity Overview]{.underline}**

**Harborview Capital Partners LLC** is a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of North Carolina. The Borrower was formed on **March 14, 2019**, and is registered with the North Carolina Secretary of State under File No. **1923847**. The Borrower\'s principal office is located at **400 West Main Street, Suite 310, Durham, NC 27701**.

The Borrower was formed as a single-purpose entity for the acquisition, development, construction, ownership, and operation of the real property located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701 (Parcel IDs: 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102), commonly known as \"The Piedmont at Brightleaf\" (the \"Project\"). The current net worth of the Borrower entity is approximately **\$14,200,000** based on the book value of its assets and liabilities as of the most recent reporting period.

While the Borrower was formed as a single-purpose entity and operates exclusively in connection with the Project, the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of the Borrower (as excerpted in Section 2 below) does not currently include provisions for an independent director or independent manager, nor does it contain separateness covenants customarily associated with single-purpose entity structures in commercial real estate finance transactions. Additionally, as detailed in Section 1.2 below, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, which holds a 28% membership interest in the Borrower, is an affiliate of Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, the mezzanine lender to the Project, and both entities are under the common control of Thomas R. Chen. This structural relationship warrants review in the context of SPE separateness analysis.

**[1.2 Member Structure (Ownership Chart)]{.underline}**

The following sets forth the ownership structure of Harborview Capital Partners LLC as of the date hereof, presented in two tiers reflecting direct membership interests in the Borrower and the control structure of the entity members.

**Tier 1 --- Members of Harborview Capital Partners LLC**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Tier 2 --- Control of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC**

Brightleaf Investors Group LLC is a North Carolina limited liability company with its principal office in Durham, North Carolina. The Managing Member of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC is **Thomas R. Chen**. The other members of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC consist of a group of local high-net-worth investors whose identities are available upon request under separate confidentiality agreement.

**Tier 2 --- Affiliate Relationship (Critical Notation)**

**Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC** (NC LLC, NC SOS File No. **2103988**) is an affiliate of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC. Both entities are under the **common control of Thomas R. Chen**, who serves as the Managing Member of both Brightleaf Investors Group LLC and Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC.

Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC is providing a **\$9,200,000 mezzanine loan** to the Borrower at a fixed rate of **12.50% per annum**, secured by a **pledge of 100% of the membership interests** in the Borrower. The mezzanine loan matures coterminous with the senior construction loan from Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. The Borrower\'s capital structure, accordingly, includes both an equity member (Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, 28%) and a mezzanine lender (Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC), each under the common control of the same individual.

*Note: The mezzanine loan from Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC is secured by a pledge of 100% of the membership interests in the Borrower. An intercreditor agreement between Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. and Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC has been negotiated but is not yet executed as of the date hereof.*

**Notation on Guarantors**

The following individuals have agreed to serve as personal guarantors in connection with the senior construction loan from Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.:

**Elena Vasquez-Torres** (62% Member / Managing Member) --- Personal guarantor. Approximate net worth: **\$29.8 million** (liquid assets: \$6.1 million; real estate holdings: \$19.4 million; other assets: \$4.3 million). Ms. Vasquez-Torres has 22 years of commercial real estate development experience and is a resident of Durham, North Carolina.

**Reginald K. Osei** (10% Member) --- Personal guarantor. Approximate net worth: **\$11.5 million** (liquid assets: \$3.2 million; real estate holdings: \$6.8 million; other assets: \$1.5 million). Mr. Osei has 15 years of experience in real estate finance and development and is a resident of Chapel Hill, North Carolina.

Combined guarantor net worth: approximately **\$41.3 million**. Combined guarantor liquidity: **\$9,300,000** (\$6.1M + \$3.2M).

**[1.3 Capital Contributions and Equity Summary]{.underline}**

**Land Contribution.** The real property comprising the Project site (Parcel IDs: 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102) was contributed to Harborview Capital Partners LLC by **Elena Vasquez-Torres** at a cost basis of **\$8,200,000**. The land was originally acquired by Ms. Vasquez-Torres in a transaction funded from her personal resources and was subsequently contributed to the Borrower upon formation of the project entity. The contribution was reflected on the Borrower\'s books at the **\$8,200,000** acquisition cost basis. For reference, the as-is appraised value of the land per the appraisal by Ridgeline Appraisal Services Inc. dated November 15, 2024 (Appraiser: Linda M. Haverford, MAI) is **\$8,900,000**, which exceeds the acquisition cost basis by \$700,000.

**Member Capital Calls.** The members have funded the following capital contributions to date:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Member**                        **Capital Contribution**                        **Source**
  --------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------- --------------------------------
  Elena Vasquez-Torres              \$8,200,000 (land contribution at cost basis)   Personal acquisition of land

  Brightleaf Investors Group LLC    \$0 cash to date                                Future capital calls as needed

  Reginald K. Osei                  \$0 cash to date                                Future capital calls as needed

  **Total member equity to date**   **\$8,200,000**                                 
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Additional Funding Sources.** The total project cost for The Piedmont at Brightleaf is **\$56,700,000**. Beyond the member equity reflected above, the Project is funded as follows:

> • Senior construction loan (Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.): **\$47,500,000**
>
> • Mezzanine loan (Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC): **\$9,200,000**
>
> • Additional borrower cash equity: **\$0**
>
> • **Total: \$47,500,000 + \$9,200,000 + \$0 = \$56,700,000**

The foregoing sources and uses summary reflects that there is no additional cash equity contribution from any member beyond the land contribution by Ms. Vasquez-Torres. The entire non-debt funding of the Project consists of the \$8,200,000 land contribution. Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, the 28% member affiliated with the mezzanine lender, has contributed no cash equity to date; its membership interest was issued in consideration of its commitment to arrange third-party mezzanine financing for the Project, as set forth in the Operating Agreement (see Section 2.3 below). The mezzanine loan of \$9,200,000 from Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, an affiliate of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, fills the gap between the senior loan proceeds and the total project cost. No independent cash equity beyond the land contribution exists in the capital stack.

**[SECTION 2: EXCERPTS FROM OPERATING AGREEMENT OF HARBORVIEW CAPITAL PARTNERS LLC]{.underline}**

**[2.1 Preamble and Identification]{.underline}**

The following are selected excerpts from the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of Harborview Capital Partners LLC, dated as of March 14, 2019, as amended through December 1, 2024 (the \"Operating Agreement\"). These excerpts are provided for informational purposes only in connection with the senior construction loan from Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. (Loan No. CRE-2025-0342) and do not constitute the complete Operating Agreement. The full Operating Agreement has been provided to Lender\'s counsel, Ashford, Cromdale Consulting & Laine LLP, under separate cover. In the event of any conflict between these excerpts and the full Operating Agreement, the full Operating Agreement shall control.

**[2.2 Excerpt --- Article III: Management and Authority (Section 3.1 --- Managing Member)]{.underline}**

The following is excerpted from Article III, Section 3.1 of the Operating Agreement:

> *Section 3.1 --- Managing Member.* **Elena Vasquez-Torres** shall serve as the sole Managing Member of the Company. The Managing Member shall have the exclusive authority to manage the day-to-day operations and affairs of the Company, including without limitation: (a) entering into contracts on behalf of the Company in the ordinary course of business; (b) hiring and terminating employees, contractors, and consultants; (c) making capital expenditure decisions with respect to the Project in amounts not exceeding Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) individually (any single expenditure in excess of \$500,000 shall require the prior approval of Members holding a majority in interest of the outstanding membership interests); (d) executing loan documents, promissory notes, deeds of trust, and related instruments on behalf of the Company; and (e) managing and overseeing the construction and development of the Project, including selection of architects, general contractors, and subcontractors.
>
> *Section 3.2 --- Major Decisions.* Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following actions shall require the prior written approval of Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the outstanding membership interests: (a) any sale, transfer, or encumbrance of all or substantially all of the Company\'s assets; (b) any financing or refinancing of the Property in a principal amount in excess of One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000); (c) the admission of any new Member to the Company; (d) any amendment to this Operating Agreement; and (e) any voluntary dissolution of the Company or the filing of any petition for relief under any federal or state bankruptcy or insolvency law.

The approval threshold of 75% means that Elena Vasquez-Torres (62%) cannot unilaterally approve any major decision. She would require the concurrence of at least one additional member. Combined with Brightleaf Investors Group LLC (28%), the two members hold 90%, which exceeds the 75% threshold. Combined with Reginald K. Osei (10%), Ms. Vasquez-Torres and Mr. Osei hold 72%, which falls below the 75% threshold. Consequently, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC holds an effective veto right over major decisions, as no combination of the other two members alone can reach the required supermajority.

The Operating Agreement, as currently in effect, does not contain any provision requiring the appointment of an independent director or independent manager for the Company. There are no separateness covenants requiring the Company to maintain its own books, records, and bank accounts separate from those of its members or their affiliates, no prohibition on commingling of funds with affiliates, and no requirement that the Company obtain a non-consolidation opinion. These provisions are customarily required by institutional lenders in single-purpose entity structures.

**[2.3 Excerpt --- Article V: Capital Contributions (Section 5.1 --- Initial Capital Contributions; Section 5.3 --- Additional Capital Calls)]{.underline}**

The following is excerpted from Article V, Sections 5.1 and 5.3 of the Operating Agreement:

> *Section 5.1 --- Initial Capital Contributions.* Each Member shall make the following initial capital contributions to the Company:
>
> \(a\) **Elena Vasquez-Torres** shall contribute that certain real property located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701 (Parcel IDs: 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102), together with all improvements, easements, and appurtenances thereto, valued at Eight Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$8,200,000) (acquisition cost basis), in exchange for a sixty-two percent (62%) membership interest in the Company.
>
> \(b\) **Brightleaf Investors Group LLC** shall make an initial capital contribution of Zero Dollars (\$0) at the time of formation. Brightleaf Investors Group LLC shall receive a twenty-eight percent (28%) membership interest in the Company in consideration of its commitment to arrange third-party mezzanine financing for the Project and to contribute future capital as and when called by the Managing Member in accordance with Section 5.3 of this Agreement.
>
> \(c\) **Reginald K. Osei** shall make an initial capital contribution of Zero Dollars (\$0) at the time of formation. Reginald K. Osei shall receive a ten percent (10%) membership interest in the Company in consideration of development management services to be provided to the Company in connection with the Project and his commitment to contribute future capital as and when called by the Managing Member in accordance with Section 5.3 of this Agreement.
>
> *Section 5.3 --- Additional Capital Calls.* The Managing Member may, from time to time, issue capital calls to all Members pro rata in proportion to their respective membership interests, upon not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice. Capital calls shall be at the sole discretion of the Managing Member for purposes of funding Project costs not covered by loan proceeds or other available funds. Any Member who fails to fund a capital call within the applicable notice period shall be subject to dilution of such Member\'s membership interest on a two-to-one (2:1) penalty basis, as calculated in accordance with Schedule B attached hereto.

As reflected above, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC received its 28% membership interest not in exchange for a cash capital contribution but in consideration of its commitment to arrange third-party mezzanine financing for the Project. That mezzanine financing was arranged through Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, an entity under the common control of Thomas R. Chen, who also serves as Managing Member of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC. The Borrower\'s cash equity position is therefore entirely dependent on the land contribution made by Elena Vasquez-Torres.

**[2.4 Excerpt --- Article VI: Distributions (Section 6.1 --- Distribution Waterfall)]{.underline}**

The following is excerpted from Article VI, Section 6.1 of the Operating Agreement:

> *Section 6.1 --- Distribution Waterfall.* Distributable Cash (as defined in Section 1.1 of this Agreement, being the net cash from operations of the Company or net proceeds from a Capital Event, in each case after payment of all Company obligations, including without limitation debt service on all loans (including the senior construction loan, any mezzanine or subordinate financing, and any other indebtedness of the Company), required reserves, and operating expenses) shall be distributed to the Members in the following order of priority:
>
> \(a\) **First**, to all Members pro rata in proportion to their respective membership interests, until each Member has received a cumulative return equal to a nine percent (9.0%) per annum preferred return on such Member\'s unreturned capital contribution (as calculated on a non-compounded basis from the date of such contribution);
>
> \(b\) **Second**, to all Members pro rata in proportion to their respective membership interests, until each Member has received a return of one hundred percent (100%) of such Member\'s unreturned capital contribution; and
>
> \(c\) **Third**, the balance, if any, shall be distributed seventy percent (70%) to Elena Vasquez-Torres (as the Managing Member), twenty percent (20%) to Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, and ten percent (10%) to Reginald K. Osei (the \"Promote Split\").

The distribution waterfall expressly provides that debt service on \"all loans,\" including any mezzanine or subordinate financing, constitutes a Company obligation that must be satisfied before any distributions are made to the Members. This structure places the mezzanine loan from Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC --- an affiliate of the 28% member, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC --- at a priority ahead of member distributions, further intertwining the financial relationship between the Borrower, its equity members, and the mezzanine lender.

**[2.5 Excerpt --- Article IX: Transfer Restrictions (Section 9.1 --- Restrictions on Transfer)]{.underline}**

The following is excerpted from Article IX, Section 9.1 of the Operating Agreement:

> *Section 9.1 --- Restrictions on Transfer.* No Member may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, encumber, hypothecate, or otherwise dispose of all or any portion of such Member\'s membership interest in the Company without the prior written consent of the Managing Member and Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the outstanding membership interests. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Member may pledge such Member\'s membership interest to a lender as collateral for a bona fide loan, provided that such pledge has been approved in writing by the Managing Member. Any purported transfer in violation of this Section 9.1 shall be null and void and of no force or effect.

The Operating Agreement permits pledges of membership interests with Managing Member approval but does not distinguish between a pledge to the senior lender and a pledge to the mezzanine lender, nor does it address relative priority between competing pledges of the same membership interests. As noted in Section 1.2 above, the mezzanine lender (Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC) currently holds a pledge of 100% of the membership interests in the Borrower as security for the mezzanine loan. If the senior construction lender, Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A., also requires a pledge of 100% of the membership interests as collateral for the senior loan, the Operating Agreement provides no mechanism to resolve conflicting first-priority claims on the same collateral. The resolution of priority as between the competing pledges is expected to be addressed by the intercreditor agreement between Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. and Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, which has been negotiated but is not yet executed as of the date hereof.

"""Validate a .docx for delivery.

Checks ZIP integrity, XML well-formedness for every part, [Content_Types].xml
presence, and relationship consistency (no dangling rIds). Does NOT do XSD
schema validation in v1 — defer until ECMA-376 XSDs are vendored fresh from
ECMA-International.

Usage: python validate.py file.docx
Exit 0 = valid; non-zero = errors printed to stderr.
"""
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path
from lxml import etree


def validate(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    errors = []

    if not path.exists():
        return [f"File not found: {path}"]
    if not zipfile.is_zipfile(path):
        return [f"Not a valid ZIP: {path}"]

    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
        names = set(z.namelist())

        if "[Content_Types].xml" not in names:
            errors.append("Missing [Content_Types].xml")
            return errors

        # XML well-formedness for every .xml and .rels part
        for name in names:
            if name.endswith(".xml") or name.endswith(".rels"):
                try:
                    etree.fromstring(z.read(name))
                except etree.XMLSyntaxError as e:
                    errors.append(f"Malformed XML in {name}: {e}")

        # Relationship target consistency
        for rels_name in [n for n in names if n.endswith(".rels")]:
            try:
                rels = etree.fromstring(z.read(rels_name))
            except etree.XMLSyntaxError:
                continue
            ns = "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships}"
            for rel in rels.findall(f"{ns}Relationship"):
                target = rel.get("Target") or ""
                target_mode = rel.get("TargetMode", "Internal")
                if target_mode == "External" or target.startswith(("http", "mailto:")):
                    continue
                # Targets starting with "/" are package-absolute (root-relative).
                # Others are relative to the .rels file's parent directory.
                if target.startswith("/"):
                    target_norm = target.lstrip("/")
                else:
                    rels_path = Path(rels_name)
                    base_dir = rels_path.parent.parent if rels_path.parent.name == "_rels" else rels_path.parent
                    target_norm = (base_dir / target).as_posix()
                parts = []

                r.bold = bold or (i % 2 == 1)

                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
            elif ci > 0 and right_align_from is None and ncols > 2 and val and str(val).strip().startswith("$"):
                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
            if header and ri == 0:
                _shade(cell, shade)
    if widths:
        for ci, w in enumerate(widths):
            for row in t.rows:
                row.cells[ci].width = Inches(w)
    # spacing after table
    sp = doc.add_paragraph()
    sp.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    sp.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
    sp.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
    for r in sp.runs:
        r.font.size = Pt(2)
    return t

    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.add_run().add_break(WD_BREAK.PAGE)
    return p

    p = doc.add_paragraph()

    pf.space_before = Pt(4); pf.space_after = Pt(8)

def _shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear"); shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def _cell_margins(table, top=40, bottom=40, left=70, right=70):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    mar = OxmlElement("w:tblCellMar")
    for side, val in (("top", top), ("left", left), ("bottom", bottom), ("right", right)):
        el = OxmlElement(f"w:{side}")
        el.set(qn("w:w"), str(val)); el.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
        mar.append(el)

def table(doc, rows, widths=None, header=True, size=9.5, align=None, shade="D9D9D9",
          first_col_bold=False, space_after=8, right_align_from=None):

    t.autofit = False
    _cell_margins(t)
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):

        for ci, val in enumerate(row):
            cell = cells[ci]
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(1)
            p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
            txt = "" if val is None else str(val)

            # allow **bold** inline
            parts = txt.split("**")
            for i, part in enumerate(parts):

                r = p.add_run(part)
                r.font.size = Pt(size); r.font.name = FONT
                r.bold = bold or (i % 2 == 1)
            if align == "center" or (header and ri == 0):
                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            elif right_align_from is not None and ci >= right_align_from:

            elif ci > 0 and right_align_from is None and ncols > 2 and val and str(val).strip().startswith("$"):
                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT

    if widths:

    # spacing after table
    sp = doc.add_paragraph()
    sp.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    sp.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
    sp.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
    for r in sp.runs:
        r.font.size = Pt(2)
    return t


def page_break(doc):

    p.add_run().add_break(WD_BREAK.PAGE)
    return p

tool_calls.name: bash
tool_calls.arguments:
{"command": "cd $WORKSPACE_DIR/build && cat >> agreement.py <<'PYEOF'

# ================================================================ ARTICLE IV
article(doc, "IV", "Advances; Disbursement Mechanics")

section(doc, "4.1", "Draw Schedule",
    "Advances shall be made in accordance with the Approved Draw Schedule attached as Exhibit D, which is tied to the construction "
    "milestones described therein. Each Advance shall be in the amount set forth in Exhibit D for the applicable milestone, subject to "
    "retention of the Retainage in accordance with Section 4.4 and to the adjustments contemplated by Section 2.2 and Section 4.6. If "
    "the Commitment Amount is reduced pursuant to Section 2.2, Exhibit D shall be conformed as provided in Section 2.2(b) and in Exhibit D. "
    "Lender shall not be obligated to make any Advance in excess of the amount then available under Exhibit D, and Borrower shall not be "
    "entitled to any Advance for a milestone that has not been achieved and certified in accordance with this Article IV.")
note(doc, "[Note to Draft: Exhibit D conforms the draw schedule to the 10% Retainage requirement and to the funding of the Developer Fee from "
          "senior and mezzanine sources. The schedule as presented in the Term Sheet (Section 9.2) and the Credit Memorandum (Section 7.1) "
          "disburses 100% of the $34,750,000 guaranteed maximum price in Draws 2 through 8 and then “releases” $3,275,000 of Retainage in Draw 9 "
          "that was never withheld, and its Draw 9 components do not foot ($4,275,000 of components against a stated $3,275,000). See "
          "Memorandum Section 3.6 and Exhibit D hereto.]")

section(doc, "4.2", "Draw Requests",
    "Borrower shall submit each Draw Request to Lender not less than fifteen (15) days prior to the proposed Advance date, in the form "
    "attached as Exhibit G, accompanied by:")
DRAWREQ = [
("(a)", "an AIA Application and Certificate for Payment (Form G702) and Continuation Sheet (Form G703), certified by Architect and General Contractor;"),
("(b)", "a current construction progress report and updated construction schedule, certified by Borrower and General Contractor;"),
("(c)", "a certification from the Construction Inspector confirming achievement of the applicable milestone and the percentage of completion stated in the Draw Request;"),
("(d)", "conditional and unconditional partial lien waivers, in the statutory form prescribed by N.C.G.S. Chapter 44A, from General Contractor and each subcontractor and materialman for work performed and materials furnished through the date of the Draw Request;"),
("(e)", "a title date-down endorsement from Title Company confirming the continued first-priority status of the Deed of Trust and the absence of any intervening Lien;"),
("(f)", "evidence that all insurance required under Article IX remains in full force and effect;"),
("(g)", "a budget reconciliation demonstrating that the remaining undisbursed Loan proceeds, the LTC Equity Deposit and Borrower’s other committed funds are sufficient to complete the Project in accordance with the Approved Budget;"),
("(h)", "a Borrower’s certificate that no Default or Event of Default exists, that all representations and warranties remain true and correct in all material respects, and that the Interest Reserve adequacy test required by Section 2.7(c) has been satisfied; and"),
("(i)", "such other documentation as Lender may reasonably require."),
]
for lbl, txt in DRAWREQ:
    sub(doc, lbl, txt, level=1, size=10.5)

section(doc, "4.3", "Conditions to Each Advance",
    "Lender’s obligation to make any Advance (including the initial Advance) is subject to the satisfaction (or written waiver by "
    "Lender) of each of the following conditions as of the date of such Advance:")
ADVC = [
("(a)", "all conditions precedent to Closing set forth in Article III shall have been satisfied or waived in writing;"),
("(b)", "no Default or Event of Default shall exist, and no condition shall exist that with notice or lapse of time or both would constitute a Default or Event of Default;"),
("(c)", "all representations and warranties of Borrower and each Guarantor in the Loan Documents shall be true and correct in all material respects;"),
("(d)", "Lender shall have received a complete Draw Request complying with Section 4.2 and a satisfactory report from the Construction Inspector;"),
("(e)", "the Interest Reserve adequacy test described in Section 2.7(c) shall have been satisfied, or Borrower shall have deposited the required deficiency;"),
("(f)", "the LTC Equity Deposit shall have been fully disbursed and applied to Project costs before any Advance other than the initial Advance, except as otherwise provided in the Equity Escrow Agreement;"),
("(g)", "no Material Adverse Effect shall have occurred;"),
("(h)", "all permits, approvals and the architectural review approvals described in Section 3.12 shall remain in full force and effect;"),
("(i)", "each condition of the NFA Letter applicable to the stage of construction then underway shall have been satisfied, and the Vapor Mitigation System shall have been installed in accordance with Section 10.4 before any Advance is made for work above the podium level in the Affected Area; and"),
("(j)", "the Intercreditor Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and no default shall exist thereunder."),
]
for lbl, txt in ADVC:
    sub(doc, lbl, txt, level=1, size=10.5)

section(doc, "4.4", "Retainage",
    "Lender shall retain ten percent (10%) of each Advance attributable to hard construction costs (the “Retainage”), which for the "
    "Project equals $3,475,000. The Retainage shall be held by Lender and released as Draw 9 under Exhibit D, and only upon Lender’s "
    "receipt of (a) a final, unconditional certificate of occupancy issued by the City of Durham for all residential units and retail "
    "space; (b) final, unconditional lien waivers from General Contractor, each subcontractor and each materialman; (c) Architect’s "
    "certificate of final completion; (d) evidence of the expiration of the lien filing period under N.C.G.S. Chapter 44A (being 120 days "
    "from the date of last furnishing of labor or materials to the Property) or, in the alternative, the posting of a lien bond in form and "
    "amount satisfactory to Lender; (e) a final title date-down endorsement; and (f) evidence of compliance with each condition of the "
    "NFA Letter. Lender may, in its discretion, apply all or any portion of the Retainage to cure any Default, to complete any incomplete "
    "work, or to pay any Lien asserted against the Property.")

section(doc, "4.5", "Equity First",
    "Borrower’s equity in the Project, consisting of the Land (at the Contribution Value) and the LTC Equity Deposit, shall be fully "
    "invested in the Project before any Advance other than the initial Advance is made. Lender shall disburse the LTC Equity Deposit "
    "in accordance with the Equity Escrow Agreement and prior to, and in any event not later than the corresponding, Advances of Loan "
    "proceeds. Borrower shall not be entitled to any reimbursement of its equity contribution from Loan proceeds.")

section(doc, "4.6", "Cost Overruns",
    "If at any time Lender determines that the undisbursed portion of the Loan, together with the undisbursed LTC Equity Deposit and "
    "Borrower’s other committed funds, is insufficient to complete the Project in accordance with the Approved Plans and the Approved "
    "Budget (a “Cost Overrun”), Lender shall notify Borrower, and Borrower shall, within ten (10) Business Days after such notice, deposit "
    "with Lender funds sufficient to fund such Cost Overrun. Funds deposited under this Section 4.6 shall be disbursed before any further "
    "Advance and shall not be repaid to Borrower except from amounts remaining after completion. Borrower shall not fund a Cost Overrun "
    "with the proceeds of the Mezzanine Loan, any other Indebtedness, or any Affiliate loan without Lender’s prior written consent. "
    "Borrower’s failure to fund a Cost Overrun shall constitute an Event of Default and shall entitle Lender to exercise its rights under "
    "the Completion Guaranty.")

section(doc, "4.7", "Inspections and Retainage of Advances",
    "Lender may, at Borrower’s expense, cause the Construction Inspector to inspect the Property and the Project prior to authorizing "
    "each Advance and at such other times as Lender may reasonably determine. Lender shall use commercially reasonable efforts to process "
    "each complete Draw Request within ten (10) Business Days after receipt. Lender may withhold any Advance, in whole or in part, if "
    "(a) the work covered by the Draw Request has not been completed in accordance with the Approved Plans, (b) the Construction "
    "Inspector’s report does not support the requested percentage of completion, (c) a Lien has been asserted against the Property, "
    "(d) the cost to complete exceeds the remaining sources of funds, or (e) any other condition in this Article IV has not been satisfied.")

section(doc, "4.8", "Lender Advances; Limitations",
    "If Borrower fails to perform any obligation required to be performed as a condition to an Advance, Lender may, at its option and "
    "after five (5) Business Days’ prior written notice to Borrower (or without notice if an Event of Default exists), perform such "
    "obligation or advance funds directly to the applicable contractor, subcontractor, materialman or governmental authority, and any "
    "amounts so advanced shall constitute part of the Obligations, shall bear interest at the Default Rate from the date advanced, and "
    "shall be secured by the Security Documents. Lender shall not be obligated to make any Advance (a) after the Construction Maturity "
    "Date except for the release of Retainage in accordance with Section 4.4, or (b) in excess of the Commitment Amount.")

section(doc, "4.9", "Advances Not a Waiver",
    "No Advance shall constitute a waiver of any condition, Default or Event of Default, whether or not known to Lender, and no Advance "
    "shall be deemed an approval of the work, materials or costs for which it is made.")

section(doc, "4.10", "Interest Reserve Account Mechanics",
    "Lender shall maintain the Interest Reserve Account on its books. On each interest payment date during the Construction Period, "
    "Lender shall apply funds in the Interest Reserve Account to accrued interest, and Borrower shall pay any deficiency in accordance "
    "with Section 2.7(d). Borrower hereby grants Lender a security interest in the Interest Reserve Account, the Interest Reserve "
    "Contingency Escrow and the Equity Escrow Account and all funds therein as additional collateral for the Obligations, and Lender may "
    "apply such funds upon the occurrence of an Event of Default. Lender shall provide Borrower with a monthly statement of the Interest "
    "Reserve Account.")

section(doc, "4.11", "Title Bring-Down",
    "Borrower shall cause Title Company to deliver a date-down endorsement to Lender with each Draw Request and at such other times as "
    "Lender may request, and shall bear the cost of such endorsements. If any endorsement discloses a Lien, encumbrance or other matter "
    "not constituting a Permitted Exception, Borrower shall, within ten (10) Business Days (or such shorter period as Lender may require), "
    "cause such matter to be removed, bonded over or otherwise addressed to Lender’s satisfaction.")

section(doc, "4.12", "Lien Waivers",
    "Borrower shall obtain and deliver to Lender conditional partial lien waivers with each Draw Request and unconditional partial lien "
    "waivers for the preceding period, in each case from General Contractor and each subcontractor and materialman having a contract "
    "with Borrower or General Contractor in excess of $50,000. Borrower shall not make any payment to General Contractor or any "
    "subcontractor for work that is not covered by a lien waiver delivered to Lender.")

section(doc, "4.13", "Change Orders",
    "Borrower shall not approve or permit any change order, change directive, field order or other modification of the Approved Plans or "
    "the Construction Contract without Lender’s prior written consent if such change (a) individually or in the aggregate exceeds "
    "$250,000, (b) reduces the scope, quality or quantity of the Improvements, (c) affects the structural, mechanical, electrical or "
    "life-safety systems, (d) affects the Vapor Mitigation System or any other element of the NFA compliance, or (e) would cause the "
    "Project to exceed the guaranteed maximum price or the Approved Budget. Borrower shall deliver a change order log with each monthly "
    "construction report. Change orders requiring Architectural Review Committee approval under the Declaration shall not be submitted "
    "for Lender’s consent until such approval (or deemed approval) has been obtained.")

section(doc, "4.14", "Sufficiency of Funds; Completion",
    "Borrower acknowledges that the Approved Budget and the Approved Draw Schedule are based on the guaranteed maximum price of the "
    "Construction Contract and that the Loan, together with the LTC Equity Deposit and Borrower’s other committed funds, is sufficient "
    "to complete the Project. Borrower shall complete the Project in accordance with the Approved Plans on or before the Completion Date "
    "(as defined in the Completion Guaranty), free and clear of all Liens other than Permitted Exceptions, and shall fund all costs of "
    "completion in excess of the Loan proceeds and Borrower’s committed funds.")

    "Borrower shall deliver to Lender: (a) monthly construction progress reports in accordance with Section 8.7, within fifteen (15) days "
    "after the end of each calendar month during the Construction Period and until Substantial Completion; (b) quarterly unaudited "
    "financial statements of Borrower, within forty-five (45) days after the end of each fiscal quarter; (c) annual audited financial "
    "statements of Borrower prepared by a nationally or regionally recognized independent certified public accounting firm, within one "
    "hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year; (d) annual personal financial statements of each Guarantor and annual "
    "federal income tax returns of Borrower and each Guarantor, within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year; "
    "(e) quarterly guarantor liquidity certifications within forty-five (45) days after the end of each fiscal quarter; (f) annual net "

    "notices, permits, governmental correspondence and regulatory communications relating to the Property or the Project, promptly upon "
    "receipt; and (h) such other financial information as Lender may reasonably request.")

    "Borrower and General Contractor; (b) a budget reconciliation comparing actual and committed costs to the Approved Budget by line "

    "(f) the Interest Reserve reconciliation required under Section 2.7(f). Borrower shall promptly deliver to Lender any notice of delay, "
    "any notice of default received from General Contractor or Architect, and any revised construction schedule.")

    "of interest through the Construction Maturity Date calculated at the greater of the Applicable Rate then in effect and a Daily Simple "
    "SOFR rate of 4.35% per annum.")

section(doc, "8.9", "Compliance Certificates",
    "Together with each financial statement delivered under Section 8.6, Borrower shall deliver a certificate of the Managing Member "
    "(a) setting forth in reasonable detail the calculations necessary to demonstrate compliance with each covenant in this Article VIII, "
    "(b) certifying that no Default or Event of Default exists or, if one exists, describing it and the actions being taken to cure it, "

    "of the breach, by (i) prepaying principal, (ii) depositing cash collateral, (iii) contributing additional equity to Borrower, or "
    "(iv) a combination of the foregoing, in each case in an amount sufficient to cause Borrower to be in compliance with the applicable "
    "covenant on a pro forma basis. A breach that is not cured within such period shall constitute an Event of Default.")

    "For purposes of this Article VIII: (a) “Debt Service Coverage Ratio” means, for any period, the ratio of (i) net operating income "
    "for such period to (ii) the annualized amount of interest that would accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan at the "
    "Applicable Rate then in effect (the Loan being interest-only); (b) “net operating income” means gross revenues from the Property "
    "actually collected, less vacancy and credit loss, less operating expenses (including real estate taxes, insurance, utilities, "
    "repairs and maintenance, management fees, reserves for replacement and all assessments payable under the Declaration), determined in "
    "a manner consistent with the appraiser’s stabilized income and expense analysis, adjusted for actual results; (c) “Appraised Value” "
    "means the most recent as-completed or as-stabilized value conclusion in an appraisal of the Property prepared by an MAI-designated "
    "appraiser acceptable to Lender and complying with FIRREA; and (d) illustrative calculations of each covenant are set forth on "
    "Schedule 8.11.")
PYEOF

    "the end of each calendar month: (a) a construction progress report comparing actual progress to the approved schedule, certified by "
    "Borrower and General Contractor; (b) a budget reconciliation comparing actual and committed costs to the Approved Budget by line "
    "item; (c) a change order log; (d) the Construction Inspector’s report; (e) a schedule of all pending claims, disputes and liens; and "
    "(f) the Interest Reserve reconciliation required under Section 2.7(f). Borrower shall promptly deliver to Lender any notice of delay, "
    "any notice of default received from General Contractor or Architect, and any revised construction schedule.")

section(doc, "8.8", "Interest Reserve Reporting",
    "Borrower shall deliver the monthly Interest Reserve reconciliation required under Section 2.7(f), together with a rolling projection "
    "of interest through the Construction Maturity Date calculated at the greater of the Applicable Rate then in effect and a Daily Simple "
    "SOFR rate of 4.35% per annum.")

section(doc, "8.9", "Compliance Certificates",
    "Together with each financial statement delivered under Section 8.6, Borrower shall deliver a certificate of the Managing Member "
    "(a) setting forth in reasonable detail the calculations necessary to demonstrate compliance with each covenant in this Article VIII, "
    "(b) certifying that no Default or Event of Default exists or, if one exists, describing it and the actions being taken to cure it, "
    "and (c) certifying that all representations and warranties remain true and correct in all material respects.")

section(doc, "8.10", "Cure of Financial Covenant Breach",
    "If Borrower breaches any covenant in Sections 8.1 through 8.5, Borrower may cure such breach within thirty (30) days after the "
    "earlier of (a) the date on which Borrower obtains knowledge of the breach and (b) the date on which Lender delivers written notice "
    "of the breach, by (i) prepaying principal, (ii) depositing cash collateral, (iii) contributing additional equity to Borrower, or "
    "(iv) a combination of the foregoing, in each case in an amount sufficient to cause Borrower to be in compliance with the applicable "
    "covenant on a pro forma basis. A breach that is not cured within such period shall constitute an Event of Default.")

section(doc, "8.11", "Calculations and Defined Financial Terms",
    "For purposes of this Article VIII: (a) “Debt Service Coverage Ratio” means, for any period, the ratio of (i) net operating income "
    "for such period to (ii) the annualized amount of interest that would accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan at the "
    "Applicable Rate then in effect (the Loan being interest-only); (b) “net operating income” means gross revenues from the Property "
    "actually collected, less vacancy and credit loss, less operating expenses (including real estate taxes, insurance, utilities, "
    "repairs and maintenance, management fees, reserves for replacement and all assessments payable under the Declaration), determined in "
    "a manner consistent with the appraiser’s stabilized income and expense analysis, adjusted for actual results; (c) “Appraised Value” "
    "means the most recent as-completed or as-stabilized value conclusion in an appraisal of the Property prepared by an MAI-designated "
    "appraiser acceptable to Lender and complying with FIRREA; and (d) illustrative calculations of each covenant are set forth on "
    "Schedule 8.11.")
PYEOF
echo done"}
